 Soniya Hinduja is a senior writer at MovieWeb, where she covers film and television with a focus on storytelling, cultural impact, and industry trends. Since joining in December 2022, she has contributed in-depth features, reviews, and recommendations that explore the creative vision behind both mainstream and indie projects.
Before MovieWeb, Hinduja built a versatile portfolio writing for leading brands and media outlets, including HUL, Adani One, MensXP, iDiva, RedBus, and PinkVilla. Her work spans lifestyle, technology, and entertainment, with insight-driven content that connects to a wide audience.

 Action thrillers have a simple job: get the plot moving, give us a reason to care, and make us want to keep watching. A slow build can work wonders, but when a show opens with a choking murder, a botched mission, or a fight that leaves everyone scrambling for their lives, it's much easier to get invested. The best openings also do more than deliver a quick adrenaline rush . They establish the danger, introduce the characters, and give the story somewhere exciting to go.

 Prime Video has plenty of action thrillers that understand this assignment. Some kick off with a full-blown ambush, while others use a sudden act of violence to set a larger conspiracy in motion. Spy games, assassins, and revenge stories all make the cut here, with each show offering its own take on a gripping first impression.
 'The Assassin' (2025)
 Keeley Hawes Turns Retirement Into a Very Violent Family Reunion
 Why It's Great: Keeley Hawes has played a bunch of interesting characters throughout her career, but The Assassin gives her one of her most entertaining showcases of all time. The series is equal parts spy thriller, family drama, and globe-trotting adventure. It follows Julie, a retired hit woman whose quiet life on a Greek island falls apart when her estranged son, Edward (Freddie Highmore), arrives with questions about her past. The six episodes zip along , and the action never takes itself too seriously.
 How the First Scene Hooks You: The Assassin opens in Bulgaria in 1994, where a younger Julie carries out a hit with frightening efficiency. The sequence plays out in a fluid, almost continuous shot as she works her way through armed guards and reaches her target. Then comes the twist: on the very same night, Julie discovers that she's pregnant. It is an unexpected contrast between ruthless violence and impending motherhood, but it works well.
 Our verdict
 Watch this if
 You love a lethal lead with a dry sense of humor.
 You enjoy hitwoman stories with a little dark comedy.
 Skip this if
 Estranged-family drama isn't your thing.
 You prefer your assassins to work alone.
 Will you watch this?
 Yes No Already seen 
 'Hanna' (2019 – 2021)
 A Baby Heist Turns Into a Fight for Survival
 Prime Video Saoirse Ronan as Hanna in Hanna Focus Features 
 Why It's Great: Hanna follows a young woman raised in the wilderness by Erik Heller (Joel Kinnaman). Erik is a former operative who trains her to fight, hunt, and survive while keeping her hidden from the intelligence agency that wants her back. Most coming-of-age stories involve teenage rebellion and awkward school dances, but Hanna is a revenge thriller . The 22-episode run also gives the series more room compared to the 2011 movie.
 How the First Scene Hooks You: Forget a gentle introduction to the title character. Hanna's premiere begins with Erik breaking into a heavily guarded Romanian facility to steal a newborn baby. He fights his way through security and flees with Hanna while agents close in, turning what should be a covert extraction into a desperate escape. Hanna's mother dies during the getaway, leaving Erik to raise the child alone. By the time the story jumps forward 15 years, you already know Hanna's existence is dangerous.
 Our verdict
 Watch this if
 You want to see a trained killer figure out an ordinary world.
 You enjoy cat-and-mouse thrillers.
 Skip this if
 Coming-of-age stories aren't your thing.
 You'd rather skip the emotional side of a spy story.
 Will you watch this?
 Yes No Already seen 
 'The Night Manager' (2016 – 2026)
 One Dangerous Favor Pulls a Hotelier Into Espionage
 Close Amazon Prime Video 
 BBC One 
 Prime Video 
 Prime Video 
 Why It's Great: John le Carré adaptations rarely disappoint, and The Night Manager ranks among the very best. Tom Hiddleston gives Jonathan Pine a cool, watchful presence that suits a former soldier working as a hotel night manager. His life takes a dangerous turn when he becomes entangled with Richard Roper (Hugh Laurie), a wealthy arms dealer whose charm hides a ruthless business. What makes the series particularly addictive is how it lets the tension simmer across episodes, creating a balancing act between danger and death.
 How the First Scene Hooks You: The Cairo opening drops Pine in the middle of a city gripped by political unrest, where his routine hotel duties bring him into contact with Sophie Alekan, a guest kept under the thumb of a powerful businessman. Sophie asks Pine to copy sensitive documents and makes it clear that her safety depends on what he does with them. The request sounds small, but it sets off a chain reaction that changes Pine's life forever.
 Our verdict
 Watch this if
 You'd happily watch Tom Hiddleston outsmart an arms dealer.
 You love polished espionage stories full of double-crosses.
 Skip this if
 You need your spies to shoot first and ask questions later.
 Patient plotting isn't your thing.
 Will you watch this?
 Yes No Already seen 
 'Cross' (2024 – Present)
 A Detective's Worst Day Sets Up a Personal War
 Amazon Prime Video 
 Why It's Great: Many crime thrillers claim to get inside the minds of killers. Mindhunter did it first , but Cross feels even more committed to the idea. Aldis Hodge gives Alex Cross a strong mix of intelligence, empathy, and barely contained anger in this adaptation of James Patterson's crime novels. Cross isn't simply a detective who can read a suspect; he's a forensic psychologist who understands how people think, which makes his interrogations compelling.
 How the First Scene Hooks You: The first episode of Cross opens with an ordinary moment. Cross and Maria are enjoying a meal and watching a football game with their friends, including Cross's partner John Sampson. Then gunshots shatter the evening. Cross rushes toward the commotion and finds Maria fatally wounded, and she dies in his arms before he can save her. That sudden shift gives the series an immediate emotional stake and makes you wonder what the detective is going to do for the rest of the story.
 Our verdict
 Watch this if
 You enjoy crime stories that get inside a killer's head.
 You like detectives who use psychology as an asset.
 Skip this if
 You'd rather leave the personal drama out of your detective shows.
 Dark murder investigations make you uncomfortable.
 Will you watch this?
 Yes No Already seen 
 'Into the Badlands' (2015 – 2019)
 Hong Kong-Style Martial Arts Meet a World Without Guns
 Antony Platt/©AMC/courtesy Everett Collection 
 Why It's Great: Into the Badlands has received a lot of praise for its fight choreography, and for good reason. The action thriller series draws inspiration from classic martial arts movies while building a fascinating post-apocalyptic world. Daniel Wu anchors the narrative as Sunny, a warrior whose combat skills border on mythical. He may be deadly in combat, but his growing doubts about the system he serves gives the story more substance than a succession of flashy duels.
 How the First Scene Hooks You: The world-building is just as impressive as the action, and the show makes excellent use of its feudal politics and futuristic technology. However, it's the first 10 minutes that really hook you . It opens with Sunny riding his motorcycle through a field of red poppies. The striking scenery takes a grim turn when he discovers an overturned slave transport beside the road, surrounded by vultures and the bodies of its shackled passengers. It's a strong introduction to both the character and the world he inhabits.
 Our verdict
 Watch this if
 You love martial arts-inspired TV shows.
 You enjoy elaborate sword fights and larger-than-life warriors.
 Skip this if
 Post-apocalyptic worlds and feuding warlords aren't for you.
 You prefer grounded crime stories over fantasy.
 Will you watch this?
 Yes No Already seen 
 'Mr. & Mrs. Smith' (2024 – Present)
 A Deadly Opening Sets the Tone for Spy Marriage
 Close Prime Video 
 Donald Glover and Maya Erskine carrying a person with a bad over their head in Mr. & Mrs. Smith Prime Video 
 Donald Glover and Maya Erskine in Mr. & Mrs. Smith lying on the floor looking at each other Prime Video 
 Why It's Great: Donald Glover and Maya Erskine play two strangers who take on new identities as John and Jane Smith, partners in both espionage and marriage. Their assignments put them in dangerous situations, but the show's real fun comes from watching two capable spies try to figure out how to live and work together. The action is sharp, but the comedy comes from the tension between their professional competence and their uncertain personal bond.
 How the First Scene Hooks You: Mr. & Mrs. Smith gives the familiar spy-couple setup a more intimate, character-driven spin. Before introducing the main protagonists, though, the series begins with a different John and Jane Smith, played by Alexander Skarsgård and Eiza González, enjoying a drink at a secluded house.
 Their evening takes a turn when a vehicle pulls up outside. John and Jane prepare for a fight, but the attackers have the advantage, and soon, they're both shot. It's a brief scene, but it's intriguing because it establishes the fact that nobody is safe in this world.
 Our verdict
 Watch this if
 Awkward couples and dangerous assignments sound like a fun combination.
 You like your action mixed with dry comedy.
 Skip this if
 You prefer your spy stories without relationship drama.
 The idea of couples therapy sounds exhausting.
 Will you watch this?
 Yes No Already seen 
 'The Boys' (2019 – 2026)
 Superheroes Become Terrifying Before the Real Story Begins
 Why It's Great: As it turns out, superhero fatigue wasn't prepared for The Boys . The Prime Video series takes the comic-book archetypes and strips away the idealism around superheroes, exposing what might happen when people with extraordinary powers answer to big corporations instead of the public.
 The satire is razor-sharp, the action is relentless, and Antony Starr is captivating as Homelander . All five seasons of The Boys are streaming, and they serve a larger point about unchecked power and accountability.
 How the First Scene Hooks You: The opening sequence looks like a standard superhero introduction, with Homelander and Queen Maeve intervening when armed criminals threaten two boys. But the premiere soon delivers an uglier demonstration of superheroes.
 Hughie is standing with his girlfriend, Robin, when A-Train speeds straight through her, killing her in an instant. Director Dan Trachtenberg, who later made Prey , stages it so fast that the shock hits before you can process it. The casual nature of the act exposes the gap between the heroic image these characters sell and the damage they can cause.
 Our verdict
 Watch this if
 You like your superheroes corrupt and chaotic.
 You enjoy satire that skewers celebrity culture.
 Skip this if
 Graphic violence and very dark humor cross the line for you.
 You want your superheroes to actually behave like heroes.
 Will you watch this?
 Yes No Already seen 
 'Tom Clancy's Jack Ryan' (2018 – 2023)
 A Routine Intelligence Job Uncovers a Global Threat
 Prime Video 
 Why It's Great: John Krasinski's Jack Ryan begins as a CIA analyst whose financial research uncovers suspicious activity linked to a dangerous terrorist network. His desk job turns into fieldwork, and across four seasons, Tom Clancy's Jack Ryan forces the titular character to combine analytical thinking with the military experience he would rather leave behind.
 How the First Scene Hooks You: Jack Ryan's first scene features a CIA operation in the Middle East. When it goes disastrously wrong, the series establishes the deadly consequences of counterterrorism work before Ryan begins piecing together the financial trail. The episode then shifts to Ryan's discovery of suspicious money transfers, which suggest that a new terrorist figure may be building something far more dangerous than the agency initially understands.
 Our verdict
 Watch this if
 You want to see John Krasinski outside The Office.
 You enjoy smart men who can hold their own in a firefight.
 Skip this if
 International conspiracies and political maneuvering sound boring.
 You prefer your action without much intelligence-agency jargon.
 Will you watch this?
 Yes No Already seen 
 'Reacher' (2022 – Present)
 A Murder Mystery Welcomes a Very Unwelcome Stranger
 Why It's Great: Alan Ritchson's Jack Reacher is a former military police investigator who travels light, keeps his own counsel, and has little patience for bullies. The series adapts Lee Child's best-selling action thriller novels into a show built around investigations, sharp deductions, memorable villains, and fights that make full use of Reacher's imposing size.
 How the First Scene Hooks You: Reacher begins with the messy disposal of a dead body under cover of darkness. It then cuts to daylight, when Reacher walks into Margrave, Georgia, looking like a stranger with nowhere to be. He stops at a diner for a slice of peach pie, only to find himself surrounded by police and arrested for murder. The transition from a concealed corpse to an unassuming drifter in handcuffs makes the mystery irresistible.
 Our verdict
 Watch this if
 You're a Lee Child fan.
 Small-town mysteries and old-fashioned tough guys are your thing.
 Skip this if
 You prefer your detectives to use tact.
 You like your action heroes subtle.
 Will you watch this?
 Yes No Already seen 
 'The Terminal List' (2022 – Present)
 A Military Mission Becomes a Nightmare
 Close Prime Video 
 Prime Video 
 Amazon Prime Video 
 Justin Lubin/©Amazon/Courtesy Everett Collection
 Why It's Great: Revenge thrillers are nothing new, but The Terminal List stands out because of how relentlessly personal it feels. Chris Pratt sheds his usual charm to play James Reece, a Navy SEAL commander whose life unravels after a covert mission leaves most of his team dead. He is driven by grief, rage, and an obsessive need for answers. Overall, the series mixes military action with conspiracy-thriller elements.
 How the First Scene Hooks You: The first scene of The Terminal List drops you into the disastrous mission in Syria, where Reece and his SEAL team enter a tunnel system to capture a high-value target. The plan collapses when the SEALs stumble into a deadly ambush. Explosions, gunfire, and failing comms turn the operation into chaos, and Reece returns home with only a fraction of his team alive. The scene not only promises more breathtaking action later, but also gives the entire series its central mystery.
 Our verdict
 Watch this if
 Military conspiracies and a soldier on a revenge mission sound fun.
 You enjoy high-stakes military drama.
 Skip this if
 You don't fancy spending a season inside one man's grief.
 You prefer your thrillers with a lighter emotional load.
 Will you watch this?
 Yes No Already seen
